C000.about: Headless Godot render of one hex prism, the harness's own smoke test (not a game screen).

C001.none: Empty Main.tscn skeleton; there is nothing to look at.

C002.about: 3D terrain: elevation, per-terrain materials, water depth and shore, instanced grass tufts.

C031.about: Terrain blending, fog edge fade and chunked terrain meshes.

shots.caption: Default tilt: grass, plains and desert melt into each other and into the coast; the ocean fades toward black at the edge of the explored area.
Low oblique, zoomed in: blended edges between terrains while hills and mountains keep their cliff walls.

C003.about: Procedural feature and resource props: forests, jungle, marsh, livestock herds, crops, ore, sea resources.

shots.caption: Gallery map at the default tilt: horse herd in the centre, forests, marsh, crops, ore, sea resources.
Low close view of the herds and their neighbours.

C005.about: Civ 5-style UI kit: theme, tab bar, scrolling icon list, tooltip host, popup queue, screen stack, UI scale.

The tooltip host showing a Gold tooltip beside the pointer after the delay.
Popup A over the dimmed screen (B and C are queued behind it).

C008.about: Scenario runner demo: a trivial screen driven through real clicks and keys, golden per step.

shots.caption: Before any command: the founding city name.
After clicking the button: the city is now Ur.

shots.caption: Default camera: visible tiles in full colour, explored ring dimmed, unexplored black.

shots.caption: Turn 1: the human's units as coloured blocks, nothing selected.
Warrior selected and a path previewed to the destination (the panel and top bar are later tickets' UI, drawn in this golden).
Turn 2 after Next turn and a right-click move: the warrior has moved on.

C011.about: HUD: top bar with yields, turn banner, Next unit and Next turn buttons.

shots.caption: Turn start: top bar, turn banner, Next unit button with a separate Next turn.
After Next turn: new turn banner, updated top bar, units due again.

C012.about: Unit orders panel: selecting units, order buttons, attack preview, disband confirmation.

shots.caption: Warrior selected: stats and order buttons (fortify, automate, explore).
Worker selected: worker-specific orders list.
Attack preview dialog with strength, health and damage ranges.
Result after confirming the attack.
Disband confirmation prompt.

C014.about: Minimap in the top right corner with a camera rectangle; click to jump.

shots.caption: Minimap top right: explored terrain, own border, white camera rectangle.
After clicking the far corner of the minimap: the camera moved there.

C015.about: Main menu and new-game screen: players and nations, rules, game, map and advanced options, seed validation, then the started game.

shots.caption: Main menu: New game, Resume last (disabled), Load game, Multiplayer (disabled), Options, Quit.
Players tab: Babylon (human) and Rome (AI), no city-states, Babylon greyed out in the nation grid, nations in their colours.
Map tab with a non-numeric seed: the reason is shown under the tabs and nothing starts.
The game started from the chosen options: Babylon, turn 0, tiny hexagonal map.
The save list: Alpha, the autosave and the numbered autosave with turn, civ and ruleset.
Damaged save files listed as unreadable next to good ones; QuickSave loaded.

C017.about: City screen A: info, tile grid, specialists, focus.

shots.caption: The capital's city screen: header, stats, focus picker and the tile grid with worked tiles lit.
A Merchant specialist at work: the specialist row reads 1/1 and the stats include it.
A locked tile keeps its golden outline.

C018.about: City screen B: production queue, buildable list, purchase, buildings, puppet and razing states.

shots.caption: The Production tab with Warrior, Monument and a perpetual Nothing item queued; Top/Up/Down/X per entry and Buy prices in gold.
After buying the Monument: it is listed under Buildings with its sell price and a Sell button; gold fell from 500 to 300.
A puppet city: the state is explained, Annex city is offered and every production button is disabled.

C020.about: Policy screen: branch columns, adopt with confirmation step, culture and golden-age lines, why a policy is locked or unaffordable.

shots.caption: The policy screen as opened by the Pick a policy button: branch columns (Tradition first, more to scroll to), culture 50 / 15 and golden-age lines, nothing chosen.
Tradition chosen: its effects on the right and an Adopt button; nothing is adopted until it is pressed.
Tradition and Legalism adopted (gold); Landed Elite and Monarchy are now open.
Not enough culture: Landed Elite is open but Adopt is disabled and the hint gives the price.

C021.about: Diplomacy screen: civ list, status and attitude, treaty and city-state actions.

shots.caption: Declare war armed: first press asks to press again to confirm.
State after war is declared.
Peace status with another civilization.
City-state panel: influence, gifts, bullying, pledge to protect.
After gifting gold to the city-state.
City-state under the player's protection.

C037.none: IGameSession is an engine/client interface with no UI of its own; it is exercised by every scenario above.

C041.about: Flat-map cities, borders, roads and improvements.

shots.caption: The founded city: block, banner (name, production) and the territory border.
A road next to the city and a trading post on the worker's tile (yield icons now show on every tile).

C043.about: Client settings model persisted under user:// and the engine PlayerSettings options.

shots.caption: The temporary settings screen after clicks: move-on-turn-start on, UI scale 1.25. (Real options screen is C028.)

C004.about: Unit visuals: per-type models, 1 to 4 figures by strength tier, civ colour, health bar, status marks.

shots.caption: Gallery of 15 units: civilians, land units by era (1 to 4 figures), ships and a plane; red and blue civs, health bars and status marks.
Close view: Infantry (3 figures), Tank (4, hurt, promotion mark) and Cannon (3, automated mark).

C019.about: Tech screen: the tree by column and row with state colours, unlock list, research now / add to queue / remove from queue.

shots.caption: First open: Agriculture researched (green), its follow-ups available (blue), the rest locked (grey).
Bronze Working chosen: it and Mining are queued (amber) in prerequisite order; the side panel lists unlocks and the queue.
Pottery researched instead: the queue is replaced and Pottery is the current research.

C051.about: Espionage screen: the spies and the places they can go, Move/Cancel/Move here, the coup button, and the multi-spy assignment picker.

shots.caption: The espionage screen: each spy with rank, location, action and a Move button, a full-width coup button (label wrapped, never clipped) under the table for the spy in the city-state, then the places with the spies present.
Move was pressed on the first spy: Move became Cancel and the places the engine offers it show Move here.
The first spy was sent to Rome's capital: its row and the city's Spy present column show it.
The spy in the city-state is staging a coup; its button now calls the coup off.
Assign spies: the multi-spy picker over the screen with the second spy chosen to return to the hideout.

C053.about: World Congress vote result: each civ you know with its votes, the worth of its vote, whom it voted for, the verdict and Continue.

shots.caption: The result lists Babylon, Rome (two votes, owner of the United Nations, voted for an unnamed civ) and the city-state, then the verdict and Continue.
After Continue the world is back and the result does not return.

C050.about: Overview espionage and global politics tabs in a game with espionage on: spy moves, coup staging, and the relation with each met civ.

shots.caption: Espionage tab: two spies with the destinations the engine offers and a coup button for the spy in the city-state.
The first spy was sent to Rome's capital; the page shows its new location.
The resident spy is staging a coup; its button now calls the coup off.
Politics tab: status, attitude and influence for each civ met (the unmet civ is absent) and the diplomatic vote line.

C023.about: Empire overview: tabs for stats, cities, units, resources, ranking, religion and espionage; Go to buttons jump to a city or unit.

shots.caption: Stats tab: the engine's per-turn numbers and the score breakdown.
Cities tab: the capital and a puppet city with population, health, current build and a Go to button each.
Units tab: own units only, with position, health, moves and order.
Ranking tab: one table per category, best first; unmet civs are shown as Unknown civilization.

C022.about: Trade screen: offer builder for both sides, incoming trade and demand from an AI civ, the engine's hint, propose and retract.

shots.caption: Rome's trade proposal and demand wait at the top with their answer buttons; the columns list everything each side could offer.
A gift of 20 gold staged with plus and minus: the summary and the engine's hint about Rome's answer.
Our offer waits for Rome's turn: propose is off and retract is offered.
The next turn: Rome answered the gift, nothing waits and the treasuries changed.

C039.about: Incoming proposal popups: peace and trade proposals from AI civs with accept, decline, counter and decide later, and the status of our own outstanding offers.

shots.caption: Rome's peace proposal as a popup: what they give and ask, with accept, decline, ask for something else and decide later.
Greece's trade proposal after the peace was accepted: they give 50 gold and ask 20 gold.
How about something else: the trade screen opens on Greece with its offer staged the other way round for us to change.
Our own offer to Greece waits for its answer, listed under the notifications.
The next turn: the outcomes of our offers are reported (taken back, accepted by Greece).

C042.none: Packaging only (export presets, bundled data, notices, scripts); the exported build opens the existing main menu, whose goldens belong to C015.

C025.about: Translations in the client: language picker, OFL fallback fonts for non-Latin scripts, right-to-left text.

shots.caption: German chosen in the picker: the settings page and the sample keys translated, umlauts and sharp s drawn.
Russian: Cyrillic text throughout.
Japanese: kanji and kana from the CJK fallback font; untranslated strings stay English.
Hindi (36% translated): Devanagari with conjuncts, the rest falling back to English.
Thai: tone marks above and below the line.

Arabic and Hebrew sample lines shaped and run right to left from their Noto fonts, each with a Latin word and digits inside (the settings page on the left is not mirrored here: the harness has no window to flip).

C013.about: Notification list and popup alerts: demand, city conquered, review of informational alerts, clickable notifications.

shots.caption: Rome's demand as a modal popup: accept, refuse or decide later; informational alerts wait under Review alerts.

Review alerts: the welcome alert, informational, with only an OK.
A put-off friendship offer, back in the review with accept and decline.
The notification list open with its category summary; clicking the city row centred the camera on the city.

After One more turn the world is playable again on the next turn.
The defeat screen (scenario defeat): the game goes on without you; keep watching or go to the main menu.

C028.about: Options screen: engine options, UI scale, sound, window mode, scroll speed, edge-scroll and map toggles, asset pack, key rebinding persisted and used on the game screen.

The key bindings while rebinding: the End turn key button shows ... and the other actions keep their keys
The key bindings after rebinding: End turn now shows E, the other actions keep their default keys

The same gallery with Show tile yields switched off: the icons are gone, everything else unchanged.

Workers tutorial shown after tutorials were switched back on and the seen list was reset.

The in-game menu: resume, save, load, new game, victory status, options, resign and main menu
